root_cause_label: Premature DB Access Caused WAL Deletion
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent opened the database with the standard sqlite3 CLI (without read-only precautions) before inspecting the WAL file content, causing SQLite to treat the malformed WAL as a leftover and delete it, after which the agent spent the remaining 83 steps in a futile filesystem search loop.
t_err_evidence: Step 3: Agent runs 'sqlite3 main.db .schema' without first inspecting the WAL file structure. The task warned the WAL was corrupted/encrypted, but the agent accessed the DB normally, which triggered SQLite to clean up the malformed WAL file.
t_commit_evidence: Step 7: 'ls -la' confirms the WAL file has vanished from the filesystem. At this point the WAL data is permanently lost and recovery is impossible given the agent's subsequent behavior.
t_surface_evidence: Step 6: 'od -A x -t x1z -v main.db-wal | head -20' returns 'od: main.db-wal: No such file or directory' — the WAL file has already been deleted, providing the first visible error signal.
trigger_explanation: The agent opened the SQLite database using the standard CLI (sqlite3 main.db) before examining the WAL file byte structure. Because the WAL file had a corrupted/encrypted header, SQLite treated it as a stale leftover during the database open and deleted it. A correct approach would have been to first inspect the WAL file in read-only or binary mode before any sqlite3 connection was established.
